jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist IV
jobs.description:
**Position Description**
------------------------

  

  

**SUMMARY OF POSITION**
The Environmental Health Bureau sits within the County of Monterey’s Department of Health and consists of seven major environmental health regulatory programs: Healthy Housing Services, Consumer Health Protection Services, Drinking Water Protection Services, Environmental Health Review (Land Use) Services, Hazardous Materials Management Services, Recycling and Resource Recovery Services, and Solid Waste Management Services.  

The Environmental Health Bureau is seeking to fill one full\-time Environmental Health Specialist IV (EHS IV) for the Healthy Housing Services program.  

The Healthy Housing Services program is responsible for ensuring safe and healthy living environments through the inspection and enforcement of state and local housing regulations for residential rental housing, employee housing, detention facilities, and other regulated facilities. The program investigates housing complaints, addresses substandard housing conditions, conducts vector control and agricultural field toilet inspections, supports the Childhood Lead Poisoning Prevention Program, and performs other environmental health activities designed to protect community health and prevent environmental health hazards.  

The EHS IV is a supervisory/leadership position whose primary responsibility is to actively support the Director of Environmental Health's goals and vision by performing supervisory tasks such as administrative oversight and quality assurance of environmental health programs. Subordinate staff provide enforcement of environmental public health laws by conducting field inspections, project reviews and report writing. This role is to ensure activities are completed by providing timely feedback to staff while reviewing their work, spotting trends, and ensuring proper follow\-up. The EHS IV guides the team to effectively meet performance measures and maintain high standards of practice. Several programs also include grant funded projects where substantive administrative, contract policy and technical issues require specialized analysis, strategic planning, stakeholder collaboration, program recommendation and public outreach. This position is responsible for managing their program by utilizing team resources efficiently, thorough planning, delegating tasks to staff, monitoring progress and frequent communication. **As of October 11, 2023, the Health Department offers up to a $10,000 signing bonus to candidates hired into regular full\-time positions for this classification from this recruitment.** *The County of Monterey is committed to honoring the service and sacrifice of veterans and eligible military spouses and awards veterans’ preference points for this recruitment. To learn more about the eligibility requirements and the process, be sure to read the* ***Hiring Preference for Veterans******and Eligible Military Spouses*** *section located towards the end of this job flyer.* *The Eligible List established by this recruitment process will be used to fill current and future vacancies, both regular and temporary, as they arise.*
**Examples of Duties**
----------------------


* Plans, schedules, assigns and evaluates the work of an environmental health staff; reviews inspection and investigation reports prepared by staff.
* In a geographic district, represents the Division in all program areas to public bodies and private groups within the district; performs inspections and investigations as necessary, acts as a liaison to a variety of agencies on matters relating to the district.
* Monitors and coordinates the inspection, investigation and enforcement activities of the staff; accompanies staff in field investigations to insure consistency, completeness and conformity to laws and regulations.
* Trains staff in all laws, ordinances and regulations, policies and procedures relating to environmental health programs.
* Develops, interprets and implements policies, regulations, procedures and programs for the unit or district; identifies operational problems and recommends solutions.
* May perform the most complex and sensitive investigations or studies involving potential violations of environmental health laws, rules and regulations; prepares reports of findings, recommends legal action and prepares materials for use in legal actions.
* May act as liaison to other governmental agencies and represents the Division in responding to inquiries or providing information to the public, business and other interested groups.

  

**Physical and Sensory Requirements:*** Tolerate rodents and insects such as rates, mice and cockroaches; and substandard dwellings with unsanitary or hazardous conditions such as septic failures, accumulated garbage or animal waste.
* Work with potentially hostile individuals in volatile situations.


To view the complete job description, please visit the Monterey County website: Environmental Health Specialist IV **THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE**
Will have a proven track record demonstrating the following knowledge, skills, and abilities: **Thorough Knowledge of:*** Federal, state and local laws, regulations and procedures governing environmental health.
* Principles, methods, technology and equipment applied in inspection, analysis and enforcement of environmental health regulations.
* Principles and practices of effective supervision.
 **Working Knowledge of:*** Engineering, chemistry, microbiology, biology, epidemiology, hydrology and geology relating to environmental health programs.
 **Skill and Ability to:*** Write effectively to prepare complex written reports, correspondence and memoranda.
* Speak effectively to individuals and groups.
* Supervise, train and evaluate professional and technical environmental health staff.
* Detect unsanitary conditions and potential public health risks.

jobs.title: Principal Environmental Scientist – Contaminated Land - Relocate to Darwin
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

"What excites me most about working in the Northern Territory is the opportunity to be part of its growth story. The scale of projects, the diversity of challenges, and the trust placed in people to lead creates an environment where professional development happens faster than anywhere else I've experienced." Matt Ryan, Team Manager \- Environment, NT

**Come grow with us.**


AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping industries, clients and governments meet their environmental responsibilities while protecting the natural environment. We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. We focus on preserving habitats, water quality, stakeholder engagement and cultural resources, promoting a holistic approach to environmental impact management at every project stage.


We are seeking an experienced contaminated land professional to join our Environment team in Darwin. This is a senior role suited to someone who enjoys solving complex environmental challenges, delivering high\-quality technical work and providing trusted advice to clients.


You will work across a diverse range of projects in the Northern Territory and nationally, supporting clients across Defence, infrastructure, government, energy, resources and property. The role offers the opportunity to combine hands\-on technical work with project leadership, client engagement and contribution to the continued growth of our contaminated land practice.

*Considering a move to Darwin? With its tropical lifestyle, vibrant waterfront precinct, strong sense of community and easy access to some of Australia’s most remarkable natural landscapes, Darwin offers a unique place to live and work. Relocation assistance is available to help support your move.*

**How you’ll make a difference**

* Lead and deliver contaminated land investigations, assessments and remediation projects.
* Provide senior technical advice on complex contaminated land and environmental management matters.
* Prepare and review technical reports, proposals, tender submissions and client correspondence.
* Develop investigation strategies, conceptual site models, sampling programs and remediation approaches.
* Manage projects from initial scoping through to delivery, maintaining a strong focus on quality, safety, budget and program.
* Build trusted relationships with clients, regulators, contractors and internal project teams.
* Provide technical guidance, review and mentoring to support the development of other professionals.
* Contribute to business development and help identify new project and client opportunities.

 **Qualifications** **The qualities that help you thrive**


The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

* Approximately 10 or more years of experience in contaminated land consulting, environmental science, environmental engineering, hydrogeology or a related field.
* Strong technical knowledge of contaminated land investigation, assessment, remediation and environmental risk management.
* Experience planning and delivering field investigations and preparing high\-quality technical reports.
* A sound understanding of relevant contaminated land legislation, regulatory requirements, industry standards and guidance.
* Experience managing projects, budgets, programs, subcontractors and technical deliverables.
* The ability to provide clear, practical advice on complex environmental issues.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with confidence engaging clients, regulators and multidisciplinary teams.
* An interest in supporting business development and building long\-term client relationships.
* Appropriate tertiary qualifications in environmental science, environmental engineering, geology, hydrogeology or a related discipline.
* Ability to obtain and maintain an Australian Government security clearance are required due to the Defence\-related nature of some projects.

 **Additional Information** **Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?**


We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.


Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.


Learn more about life at AECOM: LinkedIn, Facebook , Instagram, X, YouTube \- explore our AECOM voices, employee stories, latest projects, and much more!

**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**  

"What excites me most about working in the Northern Territory is the opportunity to be part of its growth story. The scale of projects, the diversity of challenges, and the trust placed in people to lead creates an environment where professional development happens faster than anywhere else I've experienced." Matt Ryan, Team Manager \- Environment, NT

**Come grow with us.**


AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping industries, clients and governments meet their environmental responsibilities while protecting the natural environment. We provide advisory and technical services to ensure compliance, manage impacts, and reduce risks, including obtaining permits and approvals, decommissioning and restoring contaminated sites, and tackling climate change challenges and resilience. We focus on preserving habitats, water quality, stakeholder engagement and cultural resources, promoting a holistic approach to environmental impact management at every project stage.


We are seeking an experienced contaminated land professional to join our Environment team in Darwin. This is a senior role suited to someone who enjoys solving complex environmental challenges, delivering high\-quality technical work and providing trusted advice to clients.


You will work across a diverse range of projects in the Northern Territory and nationally, supporting clients across Defence, infrastructure, government, energy, resources and property. The role offers the opportunity to combine hands\-on technical work with project leadership, client engagement and contribution to the continued growth of our contaminated land practice.

*Considering a move to Darwin? With its tropical lifestyle, vibrant waterfront precinct, strong sense of community and easy access to some of Australia’s most remarkable natural landscapes, Darwin offers a unique place to live and work. Relocation assistance is available to help support your move.*

**How you’ll make a difference**

* Lead and deliver contaminated land investigations, assessments and remediation projects.
* Provide senior technical advice on complex contaminated land and environmental management matters.
* Prepare and review technical reports, proposals, tender submissions and client correspondence.
* Develop investigation strategies, conceptual site models, sampling programs and remediation approaches.
* Manage projects from initial scoping through to delivery, maintaining a strong focus on quality, safety, budget and program.
* Build trusted relationships with clients, regulators, contractors and internal project teams.
* Provide technical guidance, review and mentoring to support the development of other professionals.
* Contribute to business development and help identify new project and client opportunities.

 **Qualifications** **The qualities that help you thrive**


The following qualifications and experience are highly desired, but if you don’t tick all the boxes you could still be a perfect fit for this role. Please apply, all applications will be considered.

* Approximately 10 or more years of experience in contaminated land consulting, environmental science, environmental engineering, hydrogeology or a related field.
* Strong technical knowledge of contaminated land investigation, assessment, remediation and environmental risk management.
* Experience planning and delivering field investigations and preparing high\-quality technical reports.
* A sound understanding of relevant contaminated land legislation, regulatory requirements, industry standards and guidance.
* Experience managing projects, budgets, programs, subcontractors and technical deliverables.
* The ability to provide clear, practical advice on complex environmental issues.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with confidence engaging clients, regulators and multidisciplinary teams.
* An interest in supporting business development and building long\-term client relationships.
* Appropriate tertiary qualifications in environmental science, environmental engineering, geology, hydrogeology or a related discipline.
* Ability to obtain and maintain an Australian Government security clearance are required due to the Defence\-related nature of some projects.

 **Additional Information** **Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?**


We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including those with disabilities, additional health or mental health needs, and/or neurodiverse conditions. If you require any adjustments during the hiring process, please let us know.


Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
